verdict.rationale: Turso documents database branching: a separate copy created from an existing database, so you can make changes without affecting the original. It can also be automated to create a database per pull request, which lets developers test schema changes in isolation. Nothing in the pack shows a way to merge branch schema back into production, deploy requests, or online/non-locking DDL; PITR is recovery after the fact, not safe rollout. Missing for 10: branch-to-production merge or schema diff/promotion, deploy-request workflow, online non-blocking DDL, independent hands-on corroboration of safe schema rollout.

support.subject: As a developer, I can ship schema changes safely — online DDL, deploy requests, or branch-and-merge workflows — without locking or breaking production

citations.quote: Branches are useful for development and testing, because they allow you to make changes to the database without affecting the original database.
Automating branching is useful for creating a new database for each pull request.
